# Spoken 0.2.16 — Test Build 30
A new way to work inside a project, a page for everything you dictated, and a folder that receives your finished meetings.
## Workbench
- **One meeting at a time.** A project shows a path row "Project / Meeting" with one small tab per part of the meeting: transcript, summary and the other documents. The "+" menu brings back parts you closed. - **Back and forward.** ⌘[ and ⌘] step through what you opened, also across projects. - **Up to four panes.** Drag a tab to an edge to split the view. Drag the lines between panes to resize them. - **Times jump into the transcript.** A time in a summary or another document is a link that opens the transcript at that moment. - **Copy and Share per pane.** Each pane has a share menu; Copy puts the text on the clipboard. - The player sits at the bottom. The meeting details, with the calendar entry, open from a button at the top right. The project itself opens as a full page.
## Timeline and Dictations
- **Timeline.** A new entry at the top of the sidebar lists every meeting of every project by day. A meeting that waits for you is marked, and "Needs you" filters to those. - **Dictations.** A new page lists everything you dictated by day, with the newest one as a "Latest" card on top. Copy a dictation, transcribe it again or move it to the Trash. It replaces the History tab in Settings › Dictation. - **Keep dictations.** Choose Forever, 30 days, 90 days or 1 year. With a period chosen, older dictations move to the Trash, where you can restore them. Spoken asks before a change moves existing dictations. "Forever" is the default, so nothing changes unless you choose a period.
## Target folder
- **A Markdown copy of your meetings.** A project can name a folder, for example one synced with SharePoint or OneDrive. Spoken writes every finished meeting there: one subfolder per meeting with the transcript, the summary and the other documents, updated when they change. - **You choose what is written.** A checklist per project selects the transcript, the screenshots and each flow's document. - It is a one-way copy. Spoken never reads the folder back, deletes nothing in it, and never replaces a file it did not write itself.
## Models
- **Settings › Models & Providers in two levels.** Built-in speech models at the top, then one language model, with everything else under "Advanced". "Test model" shows whether the chosen model can handle a whole meeting. - **Apple's on-device text model is on hold.** It no longer steps in by itself. Without a language model, dictation modes fall back to Raw with a notice. An existing explicit Apple choice keeps working.
## Preview
- Settings › Storage & Trash has a new choice "Keep meeting audio". It is a preview: no audio is deleted in this build.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.16 (30)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
This release updates the library once at the first start; it only adds fields for the target folder. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.

# Spoken 0.2.15 — Test Build 29
Better sound while you dictate with AirPods, and fewer doubled sentences in meetings over loudspeakers.
## Dictation
- **AirPods keep their music quality.** With AirPods or other Bluetooth headphones, Spoken now records your dictation from the Mac's microphone. The headphones no longer switch to the muffled call mode. A microphone you choose yourself is always kept. - **Music and videos pause while you dictate.** They continue at the same spot afterwards. If nothing is audibly playing, nothing starts, also right after you paused a video yourself. You can turn this off under Settings › Dictation › "Pause media while dictating". - **One click to allow it.** Pausing media needs a one-time macOS permission. Setup asks for it after the three required permissions, and Settings › Permissions has its own row with an "Allow" button. It shows "Allowed" the first time music pauses while you dictate. - The microphone menu's first entry now reads "Default (device name)".
## Meetings
- **Fewer doubled sentences over loudspeakers.** After the meeting, Spoken removes the other side's voices from your microphone track, using the recorded system audio as a reference. Their sentences no longer appear a second time as "you". Your own words stay, also when you talk over each other. With headphones nothing changes. - Microphone passages that repeat the other side word for word at the same moment are dropped from the transcript, also when the other person sits in the same room.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.15 (29)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
There is no library update in this release. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.

# Spoken 0.2.14 — Test Build 28
A fix release: Teams, Zoom and Meet keep hearing you while Spoken records a meeting.
## Meetings
- **Call apps keep your microphone.** Until now, starting a meeting recording in Spoken could take the microphone audio away from Teams and other call apps, so the others in the call no longer heard you. Choosing another microphone in Spoken did not help. Spoken now reads the microphone the same way call apps do and leaves it shared. Before every release, a check on a real microphone now confirms that another app keeps hearing it while Spoken records. - **Meetings start right away.** The short "Starting…" wait before the first meeting is gone. - The meeting keeps recording when you switch the microphone or headphones during the call.
## Known limits
- **Calls over loudspeakers:** Spoken removes the echo after the meeting, but more of it can remain in your microphone track than before, so the other side's words may appear a second time under your name. With headphones nothing changes. A better echo removal is in the works. - If someone in the call sits in the same room, your microphone also hears them directly, and their words can appear twice.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.14 (28)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
There is no library update in this release. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.

# Spoken 0.2.13 — Test Build 27
A meeting release: a more accurate speaker detection model, a quick way to check guessed speakers, search inside a transcript, and music that keeps sounding right while Spoken is open.
## Speakers
- **More accurate speaker detection.** Nemotron 3 Diarization is the new default. On a real meeting with three people on the call audio, it found all three, where the previous method found two. Settings › Meetings › "Speaker detection model" lets you switch back. The first run downloads the model once (about 190 MB). - **Expected speakers are an upper limit.** The count you set for the next run is now a maximum, not an exact target. With more than 8 expected voices, Spoken uses the previous method, which has no fixed limit. - **Check guessed speakers in a few keystrokes.** When passages have a guessed speaker, the transcript shows "N uncertain" in its top-right corner. Click it: each passage is shown and played. Press Return to keep the speaker or 1–9 to pick another one, and the next passage follows. Arrow keys go back and forth, Esc closes. - **Your microphone is you.** If the microphone has one voice, all of its speech goes to that voice, and it is named after the Owner name in Settings › General. Names you typed yourself always win. - **Unassigned speech is visible again.** Manage Speakers lists speech without a speaker per audio track, with samples and "Assign to …". - **Fewer voices than expected?** The speaker panel now says so, for example "System: 3 expected, 2 found". - After a dictation, the speaker review in the notch comes back where you left it, with the names you already typed.
## Transcripts
- **Find in a transcript.** ⌘F opens a small floating search in the transcript's top-right corner. Matches are highlighted; Return, ⇧Return, ⌘G and ⇧⌘G jump between them, and accents don't matter ("prochazka" finds "Procházka"). Esc closes it. - **Meetings without audio.** Delete a meeting's audio straight from the player bar. The transcript and speaker bands stay, and Play moves through the meeting silently.
## Sidebar
- **Sort projects.** The button in the Projects header sorts by Last Updated, Name, Created or your own order. The Archive sorts by Last Archived or Name. - ⌘K opens search, ⌘N starts a new meeting, ⇧⌘N creates a new project. - Dictation history opens faster.
## Audio
- **Music no longer sounds muffled while Spoken is open.** Spoken used to load Apple's voice processing shortly after launch. That alone turned other apps down and switched AirPods to their call quality, even when nothing was recording. It now loads only when you open the meeting setup. During a meeting, other audio is still turned down slightly, as intended.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.13 (27)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
There is no library update in this release. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.

# Spoken 0.2.12 — Test Build 26
A design and workspace release: a calmer look, a transcript that reads like a document, fewer passages without a speaker, projects you can archive and arrange yourself, and Markdown documents you can edit as source.
## Look and feel
- **Calmer design.** Refined grays, clearer secondary text, consistent type sizes, slightly taller buttons and a visible keyboard focus ring. Animations respect "Reduce motion". - **English throughout.** Every window, overlay, alert and agent approval now uses the same English wording.
## Transcripts
- **Reads like a document.** Passages sit in one centered column without avatars or bubbles; the passage that is playing has a thin accent bar. - **Click to listen.** Clicking a passage plays from there. - **Your place stays marked.** When you scroll away during playback, a dashed marker shows where you are reading; playback is not moved. - **Player fits narrow windows.** The floating player switches to two rows when space is tight, and "Speakers" opens the speaker bands. The passage that is playing always stays above the player. - **Speaker changes are instant.** Changing a passage's speaker shows at once and is saved in the background. Speaker results always stay with their own meeting.
## Speakers
- **Fewer passages left without a name.** Passages the speaker detection could not place now go to the nearest speaker on the same audio track: microphone passages only to people on the microphone, system audio only to people on the system audio. They show "~ guessed" and take effect without an extra review step. - **Your choices are protected.** Names you assigned yourself are never overwritten, also when you run speaker detection or reprocess a meeting again. Picking a person for a guessed passage makes it yours; Undo brings the guess back. - **Optional voice comparison.** Settings › Meetings › Capture and speakers › "Use voice comparison for unassigned passages" compares voices first before falling back to the nearest speaker. It is off by default, because it loads a model and takes longer. - Copy, Markdown export, flows and agents get plain names without the "guessed" marker.
## Sidebar and projects
- **Archive projects.** "Archive Project" moves a project into a collapsible Archive group. Everything in it stays searchable and available to agents; "Unarchive Project" brings it back. - **Projects stay where you put them.** Editing a project no longer moves it. Drag projects to arrange them, or use Move Up/Down. Settings › General › Workspace brings back "Recently changed first". - **Move meetings by dragging** onto another project again. - **Search names or contents** with the new switch in the search field. - **Status dots** mark generated outputs that are outdated (orange) or failed (red). - The open tab is highlighted in the sidebar, and the gear in the footer opens Settings.
## Documents
- **Preview or source.** ⇧⌘E switches a Markdown document between the rendered preview and its colored source. A double-click in the preview opens the source at that spot. Returning to the preview saves. - **Project About** has one collapsible header and opens for editing with a double-click.
## Flows and Settings
- Clearer flow labels, "Run again" only when an output exists, and a single column in narrow panes. - The whole field of a settings picker is clickable. - Every switch uses the same style in your accent color, including the shortcut switches.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.12 (26)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
The first start updates the library once: archived projects get their own field, and every speaker name you already assigned is marked as your own choice so it stays protected. This takes a few seconds, and Spoken backs up the library first. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.

# Spoken 0.2.11 — Test Build 25
A reliability release for meetings: Apple's echo reduction is always on, a meeting keeps recording when you switch microphones or headphones, and every overlay menu works over fullscreen apps.
## Meetings
- **Echo reduction is always on.** Meeting recordings use Apple's own voice processing, the same as FaceTime, so a call played through speakers no longer ends up twice in the transcript. Other apps may play slightly quieter while you record. - **Switching devices never stops a meeting.** Connecting AirPods, unplugging headphones or a call app changing the device no longer ends the recording. If the microphone you chose disappears, Spoken uses the Mac's microphone and switches back when yours returns. A short note in the overlay says which microphone is in use. - **Faster start.** Starting the first meeting after launch no longer pauses for several seconds. - **Calmer notch.** The recording capsule at the notch no longer flickers when the pointer rests at its edge, and its rounded corners stay intact. - **Menus over fullscreen apps.** The "…" menu, the system audio menu, the calendar choice and the speaker review menu open while another app is in fullscreen. The project can be changed in the meeting start window. - **Progress beside the bell.** Transcription, speaker detection and flows of your meetings show their progress in one place next to the bell, including speaker proposals waiting for your decision. - **Correct speakers faster.** Change the speaker of one passage or of all passages of that speaker at once, with Undo. - **Delete Audio keeps the transcript.** Removing a meeting's audio frees space but keeps transcript, speakers and notes.
## Reading long transcripts
- Scrolling long meetings is smooth. - While playing, you can scroll freely; after a short pause the transcript follows the playback again. Pausing no longer jumps back, and a click in the timeline brings the transcript to that position.
## App
- **Menu bar only.** Closing the window leaves Spoken in the menu bar; Quit asks first. - **Agent approvals** arrive as a macOS notification instead of a modal window. Each agent capability can be Off, Ask or Automatic. - **Calendar** shows when it is not connected and can be disconnected. - **First launch** has a simpler setup wizard.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.11 (25)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
The library format is unchanged. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.

# Spoken 0.2.10 — Test Build 24
The first test build signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. From the next update on, macOS keeps Spoken's permissions and keychain access. Agents can now change your library after your approval, and floating panels are easier to read without a notch.
## Changes
- **Signed and notarized.** macOS opens Spoken without "Open Anyway" and recognises later updates as the same app, so Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility and keychain access stay allowed. - **Keychain.** API keys and agent connection keys are stored under "Spoken". Existing keys move over by themselves. - **Agents can change the library.** Through the MCP tool `library.apply` an agent can create projects, rename projects and meetings, update the About text, move meetings and move items to or from the Trash. Spoken shows the whole batch once for your approval and applies all of it or nothing. Nothing can be deleted permanently, and an agent cannot empty the Trash. - **Agent permissions.** Settings › Agents has one switch "Allow library changes" with a checkbox per kind of change. Earlier grants carry over. - **Readable floating panels.** Without a notch, for example on an external display, panels use tinted Liquid Glass. Buttons, the speaker name field and "Verwerfen" share one clear style. - **Calendar.** Settings › Meetings › Calendar can disconnect the calendar. The macOS permission itself is removed in System Settings. - **Smaller agent footprint.** Spoken's MCP connection loads about 1,800 tokens.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.10 (24)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
### One last time: allow permissions again
This update changes Spoken's signature from ad-hoc to Developer ID, so macOS treats it as a new app once more:
- **macOS asks again** for Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility or Calendar: allow it. - **Keychain asks** whether Spoken may use its saved keys: choose **Always Allow**. - **Dictation records nothing, text is not inserted, or system audio is silent**, although Spoken is listed as allowed: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the affected section, remove **Spoken** with "–", then open Spoken and allow it again. Spoken › Settings › Permissions shows which permission is missing.
Later updates keep these permissions.
The library format is unchanged. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer. The DMG is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite, the signature and notarization of the exact DMG are checked before publication. The new library changes, agent permissions, calendar disconnect and floating panels are covered by automated tests but were not yet tried by hand in the running app. The agent approval is still a plain macOS dialog (KON-247). Known open items: Outlook calendars (KON-270), Spoken in Claude Desktop and Cowork (KON-269), and Models & Providers clipping in a narrow window (KON-256). The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.9 — Test Build 23
A small fix release: MP4 recordings can be imported, outdated models are reported, and agents use far less context through Spoken's MCP server.
## Changes
- **MP4 import.** MP4 files (for example Teams or Zoom recordings) can be imported as meeting audio. Spoken uses only the audio track. - **Outdated models.** When a connection no longer offers a chosen model, dictation modes and text workflows say "Model … is not offered" with Choose Model, and the bell lists it. - **Agents.** The Spoken MCP server answers in smaller parts: short connection instructions, long texts in parts of about 8,000 characters, and shorter default lists.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.9 (23)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
### If something stops working after the update
This test build is ad-hoc signed, like the earlier ones. macOS ties privacy permissions to an app's signature, so after an update it can treat Spoken as a new app:
- **macOS asks again** for Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility or Calendar: allow it. - **Dictation records nothing, text is not inserted, or system audio is silent**, although Spoken is still listed as allowed: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the affected section (Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility), remove **Spoken** with "–", then open Spoken and allow it again. Spoken › Settings › Permissions shows which permission is missing.
Builds signed with a Developer ID will keep these permissions across updates.
The library format is unchanged. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite and the packaged artifact are checked before publication. MP4 import was checked with audio-only and video MP4 files, and the MCP response sizes were measured on the reference Mac. Known open items: calendars cannot yet be disconnected in Settings (KON-254), floating glass panels are hard to read on Macs without a notch (KON-255), and Models & Providers clips its details in a narrow window (KON-256). The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.8 — Test Build 22
A new look, a calmer notch, a floating transcript player, calendar meetings that offer to record, and reliable echo removal on speaker calls.
## Changes
- **New design.** Spoken is now black and white, dark first, with an accent you choose in Settings › General › Appearance (none, a preset or your own color) and System, Light or Dark appearance. Buttons follow one clear order of importance instead of the system blue everywhere. - **Notch.** Dictation opens one compact panel: time beside the notch, the target app, a wave and the mode below. Meetings show their header beside the notch and the content below it; the small recording indicator sits right next to the notch. Screenshot notes and the "Still in the meeting?" reminder appear inside the recording. - **Microphones.** Dictation and meetings each have their own microphone choice, both "Like macOS" by default. Virtual inputs of meeting apps such as Teams or Zoom are no longer offered. - **Calendar.** Settings › Meetings › Calendar shows your calendars grouped by account and the meetings of each day. When a meeting with other people starts, Spoken opens New Meeting with that event chosen; nothing records until you press Start. The event is picked from a calendar button inside the title field, and invited people show as "First Last". - **Transcript.** A floating player at the bottom with a zoomable speaker timeline: pinch to zoom, swipe to move, click to jump. A pencil edits one passage in place; the speaker name reassigns one passage, with Undo. - **Speaker calls.** When a call plays through the Mac's speakers, the other side's echo is removed from your microphone far more reliably, and playback no longer amplifies it into a hall. Older meetings improve after "Speaker neu erkennen" or a new transcription. - **Fixes.** Very quiet microphones are no longer treated as silence. Settings hover no longer flashes, and choice fields keep their arrows at the right edge.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.8 (22)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
### If something stops working after the update
This test build is ad-hoc signed, like the earlier ones. macOS ties privacy permissions to an app's signature, so after an update it can treat Spoken as a new app:
- **macOS asks again** for Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility or Calendar: allow it. - **Dictation records nothing, text is not inserted, or system audio is silent**, although Spoken is still listed as allowed: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the affected section (Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility), remove **Spoken** with "–", then open Spoken and allow it again. Spoken › Settings › Permissions shows which permission is missing.
Builds signed with a Developer ID will keep these permissions across updates.
The library format is unchanged. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite and the packaged artifact are checked before publication. The new design, notch panels, microphone choice, calendar settings and meeting offer, transcript player and echo removal were checked on the reference Mac; echo removal was measured on a recorded Teams call on speakers. Known open items: the panel after a meeting does not yet have the new design everywhere (KON-247); live waves move little with a quiet MacBook microphone and show the other side on speaker calls (KON-251, KON-253); attendees cannot yet be sorted by their answer (KON-252). The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.7 — Test Build 21
Cleaner meeting transcripts, echo removal and cheaper cloud transcription.
## Changes
- **Whole sentences per speaker.** Words from the microphone and the system audio were interleaved by time, so a short "yes" from the other side cut a sentence into one-word lines. Each person's sentence now stays together. Existing meetings improve when they are transcribed or their speakers detected again. - **Echo removal.** When a call plays through speakers, the other side's voice is removed from the microphone track before speakers are detected and the audio is transcribed. Spoken mutes only short blocks that repeat the system audio and keeps blocks where you talk at the same time. The recording itself never changes. With headphones nothing changes. - **Cloud transcription with separate tracks.** A provider on the internet, such as OpenAI or Groq, receives microphone and system audio as separate tracks, and only the speech of each, as compressed M4A: about 14 MB per hour of speech instead of 230 MB. Two tracks no longer cost twice the meeting. Servers on this Mac or your network still receive WAV. - **Transcript information.** The (i) button on a transcript shows the provider, whether it ran on this Mac or in the cloud, the model, the language and the speakers per track. - **Fixes.** Codex connects to the Spoken MCP server again. A failed re-transcription, for example when a provider has no credits left, can be dismissed with "Verwerfen"; the earlier transcript stays. The speaker review keeps its "Weiter" button visible.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.7 (21)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
### If something stops working after the update

- **macOS asks again** for Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording or Accessibility: allow it. - **Dictation records nothing, text is not inserted, or system audio is silent**, although Spoken is still listed as allowed: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the affected section (Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility), remove **Spoken** with "–", then open Spoken and allow it again. Spoken › Settings › Permissions shows which permission is missing.
Builds signed with a Developer ID will keep these permissions across updates.
The library format is unchanged. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite and the packaged artifact are checked before publication. Re-transcription with whole sentences, cloud transcription through Groq, the speaker review and the transcript information were checked on the reference Mac. Echo removal was measured on recorded speaker calls. Cloud transcription through OpenAI itself was not run for this build. Known open items: the speaker review can show a wrong speaker count (KON-224) and be slow on long meetings (KON-205); marking up screenshots in a call is not available yet (KON-241). The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.

# Spoken 0.2.6 — Test Build 20
A smooth notch overlay, area screenshots, calendar suggestions and more on-device models.
## Changes
- **Smooth notch overlay.** Meeting recording, dictation and the standby hint grow out of the notch as one shape and shrink back into it. Hovering opens the compact view, a click opens the controls. Two causes of stutter were measured and removed: the recording state was republished for every audio buffer, and the menu bar menu asked macOS about Apple Intelligence on every redraw. - **Area screenshots.** During a meeting, ⌥⇧A (or the dashed-square button in the overlay) opens the macOS selection: drag an area, press Space to pick a window, Escape cancels. ⌥⇧S still captures the whole screen. Both shortcuts are on by default and can be changed in Settings › Shortcuts. Closing the note card with X or Escape now discards that screenshot; "Ohne Notiz" keeps it. - **Calendar suggestions.** In Settings › Meetings › Calendar, allow access and choose the calendars to use. When a recording starts, Spoken proposes the title and invitees of the current or next calendar event; you can pick another event or edit both. Spoken only reads calendars added to macOS. - **On-device models.** More built-in speech models are available under Models & Providers, including Apple Speech for a fixed language. Apple's on-device text model can clean up short dictations; meeting summaries still need a text provider. - **Agents.** Per agent, you can allow setting changes and project creation. Every request is shown in Spoken for your approval. - **Fixes.** Discarding a new recording moves its meeting to the Trash instead of leaving it empty. Settings buttons in the recording overlay open Settings even when the main window is closed.
## Update an existing installation
In **Spoken**, choose **Check for Updates…**. Download and install the update, then allow Spoken to restart. The installed version should be **0.2.6 (20)**. Finish any recording or dictation first.
### If something stops working after the update
This test build is ad-hoc signed, like the earlier ones. macOS ties privacy permissions to an app's signature, so after an update it can treat Spoken as a new app:
- **macOS asks again** for Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording or Accessibility: allow it. - **Dictation records nothing, text is not inserted, or system audio is silent**, although Spoken is still listed as allowed: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the affected section (Microphone, Screen & System Audio Recording, Accessibility), remove **Spoken** with "–", then open Spoken and allow it again. Spoken › Settings › Permissions shows which permission is missing.
Builds signed with a Developer ID will keep these permissions across updates.
The library is migrated once on first launch to store calendar context with meetings. Builds 9 and newer can receive this update.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. This is the release app, not Spoken Dev. The test target is an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. In-app update archives are authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Validation and limitations
The automated regression suite and the packaged artifact are checked before publication. Overlay smoothness, area screenshots, calendar suggestions and an approved agent setting change were checked on the reference Mac. Known open items: an echo of the other side can appear in the microphone track when a call plays through speakers (KON-226); marking up screenshots in a call is not available yet (KON-241). The Spoken Library remains local and unencrypted.
